title: Thirteen Winters and One Slow Step
subtitle: 舞蹈艺术 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 舞蹈艺术（文学艺术与体育·舞蹈与表演）
meta: 主题语境：舞蹈艺术（文学艺术与体育·舞蹈与表演）　|　核心词汇：dance　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dance 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1945 my great-aunt ① led a dance that no company in the town would have attempted, and she said the leading was the whole of the evening. The ② dance, meaning the dancing and not the music, ran thirteen winters and stayed untaught; a dance, she said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left unlearned.

Every ③ dance in that hall had the same slow step against it, and the ④ dance at the end, meaning the one they kept for the last caller and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever asked for twice. A dance, the caller said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to lead; my great-aunt said the leading is the part that fills thirteen winters.

The musician meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the dance was the whole of the night, meaning the music and not the dancing. The ⑥ dance, meaning the music and not any of that, is the only thing in a night that everybody plays and nobody counts; dance, he said, is either something you lead or the only word that means both a dancing and a music. He said the music is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ dance had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the slow step. The ⑧ dance of the whole thing, my great-aunt wrote in January, was one hall and thirteen winters of leading; dance, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to lead. She said the leading was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dance I remember is the one at the end, which was called in 1971 and is still described as the longest in the town. A ⑩ dance, the caller said in 1973, is the only thing that improves by being led; every dance, she said, is a music that has agreed to look like a dancing. She said the music was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 舞蹈；舞（指舞厅里跳的那一支）
B. n. 舞蹈（指跳舞这件事本身，与那支曲子相对）
C. 固定搭配：lead a dance 领跳一支舞
D. n. 舞（指留给最后一位喊舞人的那一支）
E. n. 舞蹈；舞会（抽象总称，指一座舞厅的全部舞事）
F. n. 舞（指节目单上写到、被排定的那一支）
G. n. 舞曲（指乐队奏出的那支曲子）
H. n. 舞曲（抽象总称，指人人演奏却无人计数的那段）

items.q: led a dance that no company in the town would have attempted
The dance, meaning the dancing and not the music
the dance was the whole of the night
the dance had become a line in a programme
The dance of the whole thing
A dance, the caller said in 1973

answers.why: lead a dance 意为“领跳一支舞”，1945 年姑婆领跳了一支全城没有一家舞团敢尝试的舞。
dance 意为“舞蹈”，指跳舞这件事本身而不是那支曲子，它延续了十三个冬天而无人教过。
dance 意为“舞蹈”，指那座舞厅里每一支舞，每一支都有同一个慢步对着它。
dance 意为“舞”，指留给最后一位喊舞人的那一支，是唯一有人点过两次的。
dance 意为“舞曲”，指乐队奏出的那支曲子，乐师说这支舞曲就是那一晚的全部。
dance 意为“舞曲”，指人人演奏却无人计数的那段而不是别的，是那一晚里人人都奏、却无人去数的东西。
dance 意为“舞”，指节目单上写到、被排定的那一支，到 1958 年这支舞成了节目单里的一行。
dance 意为“舞蹈、舞会”，姑婆一月写道，整件事的舞事是一座舞厅和十三个冬天的领跳。
dance 意为“舞”，我记得的是末尾那一支，1971 年被喊舞人报出，至今仍被说成全城最长的一支。
dance 为抽象总称，喊舞人 1973 年说，一支舞是唯一会因为被带领而变得更好的东西。
